subject.title: fix: reject malformed UTF-8 in fetched web content responses

question: Should link understanding fail closed for every byte sequence that is not UTF-8, or should it retain declared supported non-UTF-8 web content through charset-aware fatal decoding?
rationale: The patch removes an existing forgiving path for all accepted text responses; choosing between strict UTF-8-only handling and charset-aware support is a user-visible compatibility policy, not merely a mechanical cleanup.

options.title: Use charset-aware fatal decoding
options.body: Read a supported declared charset from the response and decode it fatally, then add coverage for valid legacy-charset content and malformed declared-UTF-8 bytes.

options.title: Adopt UTF-8-only fail-closed behavior
options.body: Accept that otherwise readable non-UTF-8 pages will produce no link-understanding output and document that compatibility change.

options.title: Keep permissive decoding
options.body: Retain replacement-character decoding until a broader decoding policy and tests are agreed.

recommendation.title: Use charset-aware fatal decoding
recommendation.body: Read a supported declared charset from the response and decode it fatally, then add coverage for valid legacy-charset content and malformed declared-UTF-8 bytes.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent released work on link-understanding fallback behavior makes this the closest available routing signal.
